items.title: Nexon Geochem plans ₹1,250 crore rare-earth magnet plant in Andhra Pradesh
items.summary: Hyderabad-based Nexon Geochem has signed an MoU with the Andhra Pradesh Economic Development Board for a sintered NdFeB magnet plant at Thondangi in Kakinada district, with ₹750 crore in phase one and ₹500 crore in phase two. The plant is designed to make 600 tonnes of permanent magnets a year for EVs, wind turbines, industrial automation and defence.
items.why: No dates were given, but a domestic sintered-magnet maker would give Indian rare-earth recyclers a potential local outlet for recovered NdPr and magnet scrap.

items.title: Redwood Materials will now recycle Rivian's battery production scrap
items.summary: Rivian has widened its partnership with Redwood Materials, which will recycle scrap from Rivian's battery manufacturing on top of handling end-of-life packs. Redwood is also building a 10 MWh storage system at Rivian's Normal, Illinois plant from more than 100 second-life Rivian packs.
items.why: Production scrap is the cleanest, highest-value feedstock in battery recycling, and Indian recyclers chasing cell-maker scrap will face the same OEM-tied deals as gigafactories ramp up.

items.title: China's NdFeB scrap prices hold near highs as recyclers hesitate
items.summary: SMM's weekly review put recycled Pr-Nd at 755–765 yuan/kg, dysprosium at 1,230–1,250 yuan/kg and terbium at 5,600–5,800 yuan/kg, with Pr-Nd edging up mid-week alongside oxide prices. Recyclers were cautious about paying more, and SMM expects Pr-Nd scrap to consolidate at high levels.
items.why: Chinese scrap prices set the benchmark for what magnet swarf and end-of-life motors from India can fetch.

items.title: New South Wales consults on Australia's first mandatory solar panel recycling scheme
items.summary: The NSW government has released a draft regulation and issues paper that would make solar panel brand owners pay for collecting and recycling end-of-life panels. The state has more than 1.18 million rooftop systems and about 14,000 tonnes of panel waste a year, expected to reach 89,000 tonnes by 2045.
items.why: It is a live example of solar-specific producer responsibility, which is the model Indian stakeholders are now asking for.

items.title: E-Waste Day 2026 targets cheap 'fast tech' like cables, earbuds and vapes
items.summary: A WEEE Forum study found that only 32% of low-cost gadgets were sent for recycling or reuse, while 39% of buyers had finished with them within a month. The UN estimates 62 million tonnes of e-scrap are generated each year, with only 22.3% recycled.
items.why: Small, low-value items are the hardest category to collect against EPR targets, and their embedded cells add to fire risk at recycling plants.

items.title: Chennai workshop calls for a separate rulebook for end-of-life solar panels
items.summary: Speakers at a Consumer and Civic Action Group workshop in Chennai said India needs a dedicated solar recycling policy, modelled on its e-waste rules. With a 280 GW solar target, they argued EPR alone has not delivered safe panel dismantling.
items.why: Solar panels sit inside the e-waste rules today. A separate framework would change who pays, and what recyclers can claim.

items.title: India reports 13.98 lakh tonnes of e-waste for 2024-25, but still doesn't count the informal workforce
items.summary: Published on International E-Waste Day, this piece notes the environment ministry's estimate of 13.98 lakh tonnes generated in 2024-25, with 70.7% reported as processed. It argues India tracks tonnes and certificates but not the informal workers who collect and dismantle most of it.
items.why: Collection targets rise to 80% from FY2027-28. The informal channel is where the missing tonnes are.

items.title: Singapore's NEU Battery Materials raises $7.6M and opens an LFP lithium recovery plant
items.summary: NEU closed a $7.6 million round co-led by Shift4Good and SGInnovate. It opened a plant in Tuas that can process about 1,300 tonnes a year of LFP scrap and black mass into battery-grade lithium. Europe and US expansion is planned from 2027.
items.why: LFP is the hard case for recyclers because it holds no nickel or cobalt. Lithium-only recovery economics will matter as India's LFP volumes grow.

items.title: Ex-China terbium and dysprosium prices jump on US demand
items.summary: Fastmarkets' CIP global terbium oxide assessment rose to $5,000–8,000/kg, up 41% in a week. Dysprosium oxide moved to $2,500–3,500/kg. China's export controls keep these heavy rare earths scarce outside China.
items.why: Outside China, these magnet metals now sell at many times China's domestic price. That premium is what makes magnet recycling pay.

items.title: GM puts cathode made from recycled EV batteries into production vehicles
items.summary: With Cirba Solutions, GM turned 80 end-of-life EV packs into black mass and then more than 12 tonnes of new cathode material for Ultium Cells. The first cars built with it have come off the line in Michigan and Tennessee.
items.why: This is closed-loop proof at automaker scale. It is the benchmark Indian OEMs and recyclers will be measured against.

items.title: US lets ABTC export up to $100M of black mass despite export controls
items.summary: The US Commerce Department granted American Battery Technology Co. an exception to sell up to $100 million of recycled black mass abroad. US rules otherwise require black mass producers to sell their output domestically until August 2027.
items.why: US shredding capacity has run ahead of refining. Exceptions like this decide where black mass flows, and that affects payables in Asia.

items.title: Environment ministry's Special Campaign 6 targets 3,270 obsolete electronic items in its own offices
items.summary: MoEFCC's October 2–31 campaign includes an SOP for scientific disposal of office e-waste. It has flagged about 3,270 items across its offices, including 1,425 IT and telecom items.
items.why: Government offices are a steady source of e-waste. Campaign months are when authorised recyclers can win government lots.
